chapter: Chicago's South Side night life in the early 1920s
title: Chicago's theaters: Vendome, Grand, Pekin, Regal
summary: The Vendome was a former fraternal house with Erskine Tate's orchestra; the Grand showed vaudeville; the Regal was built later and torn down.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Well, what about the theaters? Where were they?
Well, the theaters are like the Vendome was -- that was a German fraternal house. When it caught on fire years ago -- then they renovated, it was rehabilitated and made the Vendome Theater out of it.
When you say the fraternal house, what was --
Yeah, that was some German fraternity had it. (unintelligible)
What fraternity?
Oh, a German name. I couldn't call that name because -- used to see them parading all the time.
I see. Yeah.
And when that place caught on fire --
Well, I just wondered whether it was a place that's different from all the orders and so forth used.

Yeah, well, it was -- that burned down practically. It didn't burn to the (unintelligible) but it was very strong because -- structure, and they rehabilitated it and named it the Vendome Theater -- beautiful house. Then just opposite was the Grand Theater, was built from the bottom up as a theater, Grand Theater. That was that vaudeville, had the black and white show there (unintelligible). The Vendome was strictly a picture house. That's when this Erskine Tate had this (unintelligible) 14-piece orchestra.
Which was what? Sort of accompanying the pictures?
Yeah.
And also, I suppose, that would play a sort of -- would it play by itself between pictures or anything?
It played like, you know, intermission, but they had a piano to pick out the score to go with the pictures, the big pictures they play.
But it would get to play when there were no pictures showing?

Oh, yes, they played. Yeah. Certain times they'd play, you know. And up further (unintelligible) close to 31st and State. Then the Vendome on one side and the Grand Theater on the other side. Well, the Grand Theater was built before this place that burned down,

and it was rehabilitated and called it -- named the Vendome.. Up further on the street there was a lot of little movie houses on the way up, TOBA houses. Then big cabarets came in, then the movie houses, all the way out to, say, 47th Street and State; different ones had big bands in those houses.
Where was the Pekin Theater?
Pekin? Pekin was down further on 20 -- 31st -- around about 27th Street. That was an old vaudeville house. That's where Bert Williams and all the big acts played years ago.
Well, I mean did they have bands in there?
They had pit bands.
A pit band. Yes, I see. Well, that was before you -- almost before you started playing bands on the stage.
Yes, that's right, before I started playing.
Yeah. And then where would the Oriental be? Now, wait a minute. It's the Regal and the Oriental.
The Regal -- the Regal was -- the Regal Theater wasn't built when I was there. It wasn't built.
No. No, that --
But the Metropolitan House is still

operating on the South Parkway on the other side of 47th Street. They're still operating. I was there Christmas, and I said what about the theater. Well, where the Regal was, they had it all torn down. They made a --
Oh, they tore the Regal down?
Oh, they tore that down, yeah.
Well, I mean the Regal wasn't built until the '30's, was it?
That's right.
But they've torn it down?
Torn it down.
Wow.
That's a project there.
Well, where's the Oriental. Is that
That's gone too.
Well, where was that?
The Oriental Theater?
Yeah.
That was down on the South Side. It was down further towards 45th Street, 46th Street or South Parkway. See, that --
(Simultaneous remarks)
-- when I was a kid.
